deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Prevents accidental or unauthorized deletion of critical Network Connectivity Center infrastructure. A policy should require deletion_policy to be set to PREVENT.

description.description: An optional description of the spoke.
description.rationale: Provides descriptive metadata only and does not control connectivity, routing, access, or data protection.

group.description: The name of the group that this spoke is associated with.
group.rationale: References a spoke group. Restricting specific group identifiers would require organization-specific resource names and is outside generic platform security policy.

hub.description: Immutable. The URI of the hub that this spoke is attached to.
hub.rationale: References the hub to which the spoke is attached. It is an identifier/reference argument and cannot be generically constrained without hardcoding resource names.

labels.description:
Optional labels in key:value format. For more information about labels, see [Requirements for labels](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-labels#requirements).

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Provides resource metadata and governance information but does not directly control connectivity, routing, access, or data protection.

location.rationale: Controls the deployment location. Restricting it to a parameterized list of approved regions supports data-residency and infrastructure-placement requirements.

name.description: Immutable. The name of the spoke. Spoke names must be unique.
name.rationale: Identifies the spoke resource but does not directly control connectivity, routing, access, or data protection.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the owning project. It is a resource-placement identifier and requires organization-specific project values rather than a generic platform security rule.

linked_interconnect_attachments.description: A collection of VLAN attachment resources. These resources should be redundant attachments that all advertise the same prefixes to Google Cloud. Alternatively, in active/passive configurations, all attachments should be capable of advertising the same prefixes.

linked_interconnect_attachments.exclude_.description: Dynamic routes overlapped/encompassed by exclude export ranges are excluded during export to hub.
linked_interconnect_attachments.exclude_.rationale: Defines route-export filtering for Interconnect attachments. CIDR selection is an architectural routing decision rather than a generic platform security control.

linked_interconnect_attachments.exclude_.description: Hub routes overlapped/encompassed by exclude import ranges are excluded during import from hub.
linked_interconnect_attachments.exclude_.rationale: Defines route-import filtering for Interconnect attachments. CIDR selection is an architectural routing decision rather than a generic platform security control.

linked_interconnect_attachments.include_.description: Dynamic routes fully encompassed by include export ranges are included during export to hub.
linked_interconnect_attachments.include_.rationale: Defines which routes are exported through Interconnect attachments. CIDR selection is an architectural routing decision rather than a generic platform security control.

linked_interconnect_attachments.include_.description:
Hub routes fully encompassed by include import ranges are included during import from hub.
"ALL_IPV4_RANGES" or IPv4 CIDR ranges are allowed.
linked_interconnect_attachments.include_.rationale: Defines which routes are imported through Interconnect attachments. CIDR ranges and routing filters are architectural choices rather than generic platform security controls.

linked_interconnect_attachments.site_to_.description: A value that controls whether site-to-site data transfer is enabled for these resources. Note that data transfer is available only in supported locations.
linked_interconnect_attachments.site_to_.rationale: Enables an architectural connectivity mode. Whether site-to-site transfer is appropriate depends on the network design and is not inherently secure or insecure.

linked_interconnect_attachments.uris.description: The URIs of linked interconnect attachment resources
linked_interconnect_attachments.uris.rationale: Contains references to Interconnect attachment resources. Reference identifiers fall outside generic policy scope and should not be hardcoded.

linked_producer_vpc_network.peering.description: The name of the VPC peering between the Service Consumer VPC and the Producer VPC (defined in the Tenant project) which is added to the NCC hub. This peering must be in ACTIVE state.
linked_producer_vpc_network.peering.rationale: References a specific VPC peering relationship. It is an identifier/reference argument rather than a generic security configuration.
